prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1016; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was operating a sedan northbound on a residential street in League City, Texas, when the vehicle struck the front of a second sedan, operated by Driver 2, which was stopped and facing south. The impact was low in speed but direct, with the front bumpers meeting nearly head-on. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash and was assessed at the scene; the nature of the collision and the forces involved appear consistent with the reported injury. Driver 1 was the only occupant of the first vehicle, and a Passenger riding in Driver 2's vehicle reported no injury. Responding officers and the Passenger confirmed Driver 1 was present in the vehicle at the time of impact. Scene photographs show damage to both front ends, though some areas of the damage could not be definitively linked to this collision and may require further inspection. No independent witnesses came forward. No prior damage to either vehicle was known to the parties or observed at the scene. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the first vehicle.
